answer:
**An explanation must describe the actual decision, including any rules outside the model.** In this scenario, “top three reasons” is a product requirement; legal obligations depend on jurisdiction and the decision process. A convenient feature-importance display is not automatically an adequate adverse-action explanation. [1](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/compliance/circulars/circular-2022-03-adverse-action-notification-requirements-in-connection-with-credit-decisions-based-on-complex-algorithms/)

Monotonic constraints can enforce a chosen direction while other inputs are held fixed. They can improve consistency, but the direction must be justified in context. Higher income does not establish a universal causal effect independent of debt, missingness, and other factors.

**TreeSHAP allocates a prediction relative to a reference convention.** Its contributions can help identify influential features, but correlated features and the chosen background affect interpretation. Map contributions to clear reason codes and check whether they faithfully explain the final decision, including eligibility or policy overrides. [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.02754) [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874)

Test stability under small input changes, calibration, relevant fairness measures, and examples with known decision pathways. Obtain domain and legal review of the complete notice process. Explainability is a system property involving data, model, rules, and communication, not merely a sorted list from one attribution algorithm.

**Technical details and references.**

Treat “top three reasons” as the scenario's product requirement, not a universal legal rule. The applicable jurisdiction and decision process determine required notices. US guidance illustrates that complex models still need accurate, specific principal reasons. [1](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/compliance/circulars/circular-2022-03-adverse-action-notification-requirements-in-connection-with-credit-decisions-based-on-complex-algorithms/)

Monotonic constraints can enforce a chosen direction for a feature while holding others fixed, but the direction must be justified; income effects conditional on debt and other variables are not a universal causal law. TreeSHAP decomposes a prediction relative to a background and dependence convention. It does not automatically produce legally sufficient adverse-action reasons. [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.02754) [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874)

Map validated feature contributions to understandable reason codes, audit their fidelity to the actual decision including policy rules, and test stability, fairness, calibration, and counterfactual examples. Obtain domain/legal review of the complete notice process.
